The increased pressure helps compensate for the decreased blood volume.","The membrane surrounding a cell is almost a semipermeable membrane, because water flows across it freely and various solutes flow either slowly or not at all.","The result is a higher concentration of solutes outside the cells than inside, and the resulting osmotic pressure draws water from the cells into the extracellular fluid.","When these neurons detect increased osmotic pressure by noting their own loss of water, they trigger osmotic thirst, a drive for water that helps restore the normal state (Figure 9.9). In reaction to osmotic thirst, the lateral preoptic area and surrounding parts of the hypothalamus increase drinking, while the supraoptic nucleus and paraventricular nucleus (PVN) stimulate the posterior pituitary to release vasopressin.","The vasopressin also inhibits your need to urinate and therefore enables you to get through the night without becoming dehydrated.","The OVLT also receives input from the tongue, and each lick of water decreases thirst by a tiny amount, long before the blood could distribute the water to reduce osmotic pressure. Receptors in the circulation to the liver detect the osmotic concentration of the fluid, and if it is low, they signal the brain to decrease thirst.","Those areas have some cells that detect osmotic pressure, some that respond to blood volume, and a few that are sensitive to both.","Angiotensin II also triggers thirst, in conjunction with receptors that detect blood pressure in the large veins.","However, thirst caused by low blood volume, known as hypovolemic (HI-po-vo-LEE-mik) thirst, differs from osmotic thirst, because you need to restore lost salts and not just water. When angiotensin II reaches the brain, it stimulates neurons that release angiotensin II as a neuromodulator.","That is, neurons regulating hypovolemic thirst both respond to angiotensin II and release it.","Whereas an animal with osmotic thirst needs water, one with hypovolemic thirst cannot drink much pure water.","The animal therefore increases its preference for salty water. Deficiency in sodium provokes sodium-specific hunger, a drive to consume salty tastes.","When the body’s sodium reserves are low, the adrenal glands release the hormone aldosterone (al-DOSSter-one) that causes the kidneys, salivary glands, and sweat glands to retain salt. Therefore, he was constantly excreting sodium and he needed to ingest it constantly to replenish his supplies.","Either one by itself produces only a small increase in sodium intake, but their combined effect is substantial,.","Animals have evolved ways of maintaining body water, ranging from frequent drinking to extreme conservation of fluids. Thirst","printedPage":303,"additionalStudyPoints":[],"sourceBodyWords":0,"addedWords":0,"sourceParagraphs":0}],"masterclassCount":2},{"id":"bp14-m9-3","chapterId":"bp14-ch09","moduleId":"bp14-m9-3","moduleNumber":"9.3","title":"Hunger","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":305,"printedEnd":322,"pdfStart":323,"pdfEnd":340,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hunger and satiety depend on signals from the digestive tract, energy availability, hormones, and brain circuits. The hypothalamus integrates several competing messages relevant to food intake."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module moves from normal feeding regulation to individual differences, weight control, and eating disorders. Avoid treating hunger as a single on-off switch: oral, intestinal, metabolic, and neural factors all contribute."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-3-study-1","text":"Food choice and energy balance"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hunger is influenced by energy needs, available foods, learned preferences, and sensory experience. Digestion converts ingested food into substances the body can use and changes hormonal and neural signals. The factors determining what someone chooses to eat are not identical to those determining when they stop eating. Biological regulation operates over short time scales within a meal and longer time scales reflecting stored energy and metabolic state."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-3-study-2","text":"Signals from the body"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The mouth and gut contribute to eating behavior through sensory feedback, distension, nutrient detection, and gastrointestinal signaling. Blood glucose is regulated with help from insulin and glucagon; disturbances in this system can alter appetite and health. Leptin, produced largely by fat tissue, provides information about stored energy over longer periods. No single hormone can be labeled the universal 'hunger chemical' because feeding is coordinated through multiple interacting signals."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-3-study-3","text":"Hypothalamic networks"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The arcuate nucleus and paraventricular hypothalamus participate in circuits that respond to energy-related hormones and regulate feeding. Lateral and medial hypothalamic regions also influence eating, metabolism, and related behaviors. Early work sometimes described specific sites as hunger or satiety centers, but current understanding emphasizes distributed networks and several cell types. Damage or stimulation can change feeding without proving that one nucleus alone controls the whole behavior."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-3-study-4","text":"Eating disorders and weight regulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genetic variation, environment, learning, and neural regulation all contribute to body weight and eating patterns. Bulimia nervosa and anorexia nervosa involve different characteristic difficulties and cannot be reduced to an ordinary desire to eat more or less. Weight-loss methods vary in effectiveness and can have physiological consequences. The course lesson is to avoid one-factor explanations: food behavior reflects the interaction of motivation, metabolic signals, cognition, and social circumstances."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h01","text":"Digestion and Food Selection"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The digestive system, as diagramed in Figure 9.13, breaks food into molecules that the cells can use.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the mouth, enzymes in the saliva break down carbohydrates.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Swallowed food travels down the esophagus to the stomach, where it mixes with hydrochloric acid and enzymes that digest proteins.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The stomach stores food for a time, and then a round sphincter muscle opens to release food to the small intestine.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The small intestine has enzymes that digest proteins, fats, and carbohydrates.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It absorbs digested materials into the blood, which carries them to cells that either use them or store them.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The large intestine absorbs water and minerals and lubricates the remaining materials for excretion.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h02","text":"Consumption of Dairy Products"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"At about the age of weaning, most mammals lose the intestinal enzyme lactase , which is necessary for metabolizing","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Adult mammals can drink a little milk, but consuming too much causes stomach cramps, gas, and diarrhea .","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The declining level of lactase may be an evolved mechanism to encourage weaning at the appropriate time.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many adults have enough lactase levels to consume milk and other dairy products throughout life.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the prevalence of the necessary genes varies.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Whereas Europeans who can digest lactose in adulthood all have variants of the same gene, people in various parts of Africa have genes that differ from one another and from Europeans, indicating that genes for adult lactose digestion evolved independently several times as groups began domesticating cattle .","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For other residents of the Americas, the probability of digesting lactose depends on the origins of their ancestors.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h03","text":"Food Selection and Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people have unsubstantiated beliefs, such as the belief that eating sugar makes children hyperactive.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The belief that sugar causes hyperactivity is an illusion based on people’s tendency to see what they expect to see.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another common misconception is that eating turkey causes sleepiness, supposedly because eating turkey increases the supply of tryptophan, which enables the brain to make serotonin and melatonin.","sourcePrintedPage":306,"sourcePdfPage":324,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The sleepiness on Thanksgiving afternoon results from overeating in general.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nevertheless, it is true that tryptophan helps the brain produce melatonin, which aids sleepiness.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other than taking tryptophan pills, the most reliable way to increase tryptophan in the brain is to eat a diet high in carbohydrates.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is the explanation: Tryptophan enters the brain by an active-transport protein that it shares with phenylalanine and other large amino acids.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On the other hand, the traditional belief that fish is brain food appears to be true.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h04","text":"Short- and Long-Term Regulation of Feeding"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When you are hungry, you find it hard to concentrate, and if you have been food deprived for a long time, it gets worse.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Experimenters put mice on a severe diet that reduced their weight to 85 percent of normal.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To continue generating action potentials without overburdening the sodium-potassium pump (which requires energy), the brain adjusts by bringing the resting potential of axons closer to their threshold for firing.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That strategy comes at a cost: Because the resting potential is close to the threshold, the axon produces accidental action potentials, and the brain’s processes become less precise.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Vision becomes less sharp, for example , and presumably cognitive processes suffer equally, although the experimenters did not test it.","sourcePrintedPage":307,"sourcePdfPage":325,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h05","text":"Oral Factors"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Anthropologists don’t know how the ancient people removed the sap to make the gum, and they aren’t sure why anyone would chew something that tasted as bad as this gum probably did .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most found the untasted meals unsatisfying and reported a desire to taste or chew something .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In sham-feeding experiments, everything an animal swallows leaks out of a tube connected to the esophagus or stomach.","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sham-feeding animals eat and swallow almost continually without becoming satiated .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In short, taste contributes to satiety, but it is not sufficient.","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h06","text":"The Stomach and Intestines"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In a decisive experiment, researchers attached an inflatable cuff at the connection between the stomach and the small intestine .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers carefully ensured that the cuff was not painful to the animal and did not interfere with feeding.","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) conveys information to the hypothalamus about the stretching of the stomach walls .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, people who have had their stomach surgically removed because of stomach cancer or other disease still report satiety, so stomach distension is not the only mechanisms of satiety.","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animals that lack sweetness receptors on the tongue nevertheless develop a preference for sugary foods and liquids, because of their effect on receptors in the intestines .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Distension of the duodenum releases the hormone cholecystokinin (ko-leh-SIS-teh-KI-nehn) (CCK) , which produces satiety in two ways .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Second, CCK stimulates the vagus nerve to send signals to the hypothalamus, causing cells there to release a neurotransmitter that is a shorter version of the CCK molecule itself .","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The process is something like sending a fax: The CCK in the intestines cannot cross the blood–brain barrier, but it stimulates cells to release something almost like it.","sourcePrintedPage":308,"sourcePdfPage":326,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h07","text":"Glucose, Insulin, and Glucagon"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Digestion converts much of a meal into glucose, an important source of energy throughout the body and the brain’s main fuel.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two pancreatic hormones, insulin and glucagon, regulate the flow of glucose into cells.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The brain cells are an exception to this rule, because glucose can enter them without need for insulin.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some of the glucose enters the liver, which converts it to glycogen and stores it.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As time passes after a meal, the blood glucose level falls, insulin levels drop, glucose enters the cells more slowly, and hunger increases (Figure 9.16).","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The pancreas increases release of glucagon , stimulating the liver to convert some of its stored glycogen back to glucose.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That weight gain is a valuable preparation for a season when the animal will have to survive off its fat reserves.","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the United States, we tend to blame our autumn weight gain on the Halloween and Thanksgiving holidays, but the real reason may be an evolved drive to","sourcePrintedPage":309,"sourcePdfPage":327,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h08","text":"Diabetes and Appetite"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In Type 1 diabetes , sometimes called juvenile diabetes because it usually begins early in life, an autoimmune attack reduces or eliminates the ability of the pancreas to produce insulin.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 1 diabetes requires treatment by injections or a pump to provide the needed insulin.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the restricted diet is difficult, eating disorders are common, especially for adolescents .","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 2 diabetes , which usually begins in middle age or later, is the more common type.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In Type 2 diabetes, the pancreas produces enough insulin, but cells have become unresponsive to it.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the cells are starving, hunger increases and eating increases, but the person continues losing weight.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h09","text":"Leptin"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Taste, stomach distension, duodenum distension, and insulin help regulate the onset and offset of a meal.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers had long suspected some kind of fat monitoring, but they discovered the actual mechanism by accident.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After researchers identified the responsible gene, they found the peptide it makes, a previously unknown hormone that they named leptin , from the Greek word leptos, meaning “slender” .","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike insulin, which is so evolutionarily ancient that we find it throughout the animal kingdom, leptin is limited to vertebrates .","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because a mouse with a mutation in the leptin gene does not make leptin, its brain reacts as if its body has no fat stores and must be starving.","sourcePrintedPage":310,"sourcePdfPage":328,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After all, the body makes leptin all the time, so it should have no unpleasant side effects.","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, most overweight people already produce plenty of leptin, and giving them extra leptin produces little change in their appetite .","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, later research found that extra leptin also produces little effect on normal-weight people.","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Low levels of leptin trigger hunger, but beyond a certain level, additional leptin has only a slight effect .","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h10","text":"Brain Mechanisms"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hunger depends on the contents of your stomach and intestines, the availability of glucose to the cells, your body’s fat supplies, your health and body temperature, and the availability of appealing food.","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Just seeing a picture of tasty food increases your appetite .","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People eat more on weekends than on other days, and more when eating with friends or family than when eating alone .","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"All these types of information converge onto several nuclei of the hypothalamus (Figure 9.6).","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The arcuate nucleus then controls other areas of the hypothalamus.","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h11","text":"The Arcuate Nucleus and Paraventricular Hypothalamus"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus has one set of neurons sensitive to hunger signals and another set sensitive to satiety signals.","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most journal articles refer to the first set as the “NPY/AgRP” neurons and the second set as the “POMC/ CART” neurons (because of neuromodulators that they","sourcePrintedPage":311,"sourcePdfPage":329,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"release), but for simplicity this text refers to them as hunger neurons and satiety neurons.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even the sight and smell of food stimulates these cells, produces reward, and facilitates learning to find food .","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The result is that cigarette smoking decreases appetite, and quitting smoking increases appetite.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"From the arcuate nucleus in Figure 9.21, notice the double negative: Hunger cells nucleus inhibit the paraventricular nucleus, and the paraventricular nucleus inhibits the lateral hypothalamus .","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Output from the hunger cells also inhibits areas that facilitate sexual behaviors and responses to itch and inflammatory pain .","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Melanocortin receptors in the paraventricular nucleus are important for limiting food intake, and anything that damages these receptors leads to overeating .","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have not yet found a drug that stimulates melanocortin receptors enough to inhibit appetite without unacceptable side effects.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h12","text":"The Lateral Hypothalamus"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Output from the paraventricular nucleus acts on the lateral hypothalamus (Figure 9.23), which includes so many neuron clusters and passing axons that it has been compared to a crowded train station .","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The lateral hypothalamus controls insulin secretion, alters taste responsiveness, and facilitates feeding in other ways.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An animal with damage in this area refuses food and water, averting its head as if the food were distasteful.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It may starve to death unless it is force-fed, but if kept alive, it gradually recovers much of its ability to eat (Figure 9.24).","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, stimulation of the lateral hypothalamus increases the drive to eat.","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Damage to the lateral hypothalamus not only kills the neurons there, but also interrupts axons containing","sourcePrintedPage":312,"sourcePdfPage":330,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In both cases, damaging the cell bodies produced a loss of feeding without impairing arousal or activity .","sourcePrintedPage":313,"sourcePdfPage":331,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, the axons passing through the lateral hypothalamus contribute to arousal, activity, and reward .","sourcePrintedPage":313,"sourcePdfPage":331,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h13","text":"Medial Areas of the Hypothalamus"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Output from the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) inhibits feeding , and therefore damage around this nucleus leads to overeating and weight gain (Figure 9.23).","sourcePrintedPage":313,"sourcePdfPage":331,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people with a tumor in the area have gained more than 10 kg (22 lb) per month .","sourcePrintedPage":313,"sourcePdfPage":331,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"syndrome, damage limited to just the ventromedial hypothalamus does not consistently increase eating or body weight.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To produce obesity, the lesion must extend outside the ventromedial nucleus to invade nearby axons .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Recall that rats with damage to the paraventricular nucleus eat larger than average meals.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, those with damage in and around the ventromedial area eat normal-sized meals, but they eat more frequently .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One reason is that they have increased stomach motility and secretions, and their stomach empties faster than normal.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another reason is that the damage increases the production of insulin, which keeps moving glucose into storage, even when the blood glucose level is low .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h14","text":"Eating Disorders"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A review of 15 longitudinal studies found that depression increased the probability of obesity, and that obesity increased the probability of depression , but both effects were small.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One study found obesity in 19 percent of people with a history of depression and in 15 percent of those who had","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another study found that the average adult with depression gained about a pound per year, whereas the average for everyone else was about 8/10 of a pound .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many studies have found that the children of obese mothers are more likely than average to become obese themselves.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers using laboratory animals randomly assigned pregnant females to a control diet or a diet that produces obesity.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h15","text":"Genetic Influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Studies of twins and adopted children in many countries have consistently found high heritability of body weight .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, Prader-Willi syndrome is marked by mild cognitive disabilities, short stature, and obesity, with of course variation among individuals.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A second type, monogenic obesity, occurs when a single gene causes obesity without other physical or mental abnormalities.","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most common type of monogenetic obesity comes from a mutation in the gene for the melanocortin receptor (important for satiety) .","sourcePrintedPage":315,"sourcePdfPage":333,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have identified many other genetic variants that increase or decrease the probability of obesity .","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, obesity was uncommon among them in the early 1900s, when their diet consisted mostly of desert plants that ripen in the brief rainy season.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The Pima apparently evolved a strategy of eating all they could when food was available, because it would have to carry them through periods of scarcity.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h16","text":"Weight Loss Techniques"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That statement may be true, but it means little unless we know how long they kept the weight off, or how many other people tried the plan and failed to lose weight.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exercise is important, and it need not be strenuous, but it needs to be consistent, such as a long brisk walk on most days .","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A study found that fourteen such supplements contain oxilofrine, a stimulant never approved by the Food and Drug Administration.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A placebo-controlled study found that combining semaglutide with a .","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Recall that glucagon is a pancreatic hormone that increases the release of harmful.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Small-sample experiments with both mice and humans have shown that .","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h17","text":"Bulimia Nervosa"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Bulimia overeating.","sourcePrintedPage":316,"sourcePdfPage":334,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the United States, the prevalence of bulimia is about 1 percent of cultures with a strong western influence, and cases are known where it began to occur after the introduction of American movies and television programs .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, people with bulimia show a variety of biochemical abnormalities, including increased production of ghrelin, a hormone associated with increased appetite .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After therapy that decreases the symptoms of bulimia, the body chemicals return toward normal levels .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Eating tasty foods activates the same brain areas as addictive drugs, such as the nucleus accumbens .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Over several weeks on this regimen, the rats drank more and more each day, especially during the first hour of availability each day.","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-3-h18","text":"Anorexia Nervosa"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Anorexia nervosa is characterized by a refusal to eat enough to maintain a healthy body weight.","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the condition varies in severity, estimates of prevalence also vary, depending on the diagnostic criteria .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the research agrees that anorexia is much more common among females than males, and that the onset is usually in the teenage years.","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Contrary to what we might expect of people verging on starvation, those with anorexia generally engage in vigorous physical activity.","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The American Psychiatric Association lists anorexia nervosa as a mental disorder, but depending on the definition of mental disorder, not everyone agrees.","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although most people with anorexia experience some degree of anxiety or depression, few people had a noticeable disorder before the anorexia .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain research has found abnormalities of dopamine release in anorexia, but the brain abnormalities are more likely a result of weight loss than a cause .","sourcePrintedPage":317,"sourcePdfPage":335,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the complexity of the system also provides a kind of security: If one part of the system makes a mistake, another part can counteract it.","sourcePrintedPage":318,"sourcePdfPage":336,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The regulation choice and energy balance","text":"Hunger is influenced by energy needs, available foods, learned preferences, and sensory experience. Digestion converts ingested food into substances the body can use and changes hormonal and neural signals. The factors determining what someone chooses to eat are not identical to those determining when they stop eating. Biological regulation operates over short time scales within a meal and longer time scales reflecting stored energy and metabolic state.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":305,"sourcePrintedEnd":322,"sourcePdfStart":323,"sourcePdfEnd":340},{"id":"bp14-m9-3-study-2","title":"Signals from the body","text":"The mouth and gut contribute to eating behavior through sensory feedback, distension, nutrient detection, and gastrointestinal signaling. Blood glucose is regulated with help from insulin and glucagon; disturbances in this system can alter appetite and health. Leptin, produced largely by fat tissue, provides information about stored energy over longer periods. No single hormone can be labeled the universal 'hunger chemical' because feeding is coordinated through multiple interacting signals.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":305,"sourcePrintedEnd":322,"sourcePdfStart":323,"sourcePdfEnd":340},{"id":"bp14-m9-3-study-3","title":"Hypothalamic networks","text":"The arcuate nucleus and paraventricular hypothalamus participate in circuits that respond to energy-related hormones and regulate feeding. Lateral and medial hypothalamic regions also influence eating, metabolism, and related behaviors. Early work sometimes described specific sites as hunger or satiety centers, but current understanding emphasizes distributed networks and several cell types. The factors determining what someone chooses to eat are not identical to those determining when they stop eating. Biological regulation operates over short time scales within a meal and longer time scales reflecting stored energy and metabolic state."},{"question":"Can you explain: Signals from the body?","answer":"The mouth and gut contribute to eating behavior through sensory feedback, distension, nutrient detection, and gastrointestinal signaling. No single hormone can be labeled the universal 'hunger chemical' because feeding is coordinated through multiple interacting signals."},{"question":"Can you explain: Hypothalamic networks?","answer":"The arcuate nucleus and paraventricular hypothalamus participate in circuits that respond to energy-related hormones and regulate feeding. Lateral and medial hypothalamic regions also influence eating, metabolism, and related behaviors. feeding.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"The vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) conveys information to the hypothalamus about the stretching of the stomach walls .","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":50},{"text":"However, people who have had their stomach surgically removed because of stomach cancer or other disease still report satiety, so stomach distension is not the only mechanisms of satiety.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":51},{"text":"Animals that lack sweetness receptors on the tongue nevertheless develop a preference for sugary foods and liquids, because of their effect on receptors in the intestines .","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":52},{"text":"Distension of the duodenum releases the hormone cholecystokinin (ko-leh-SIS-teh-KI-nehn) (CCK) , which produces satiety in two ways .","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"Second, CCK stimulates the vagus nerve to send signals to the hypothalamus, causing cells there to release a neurotransmitter that is a shorter version of the CCK molecule itself .","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":54},{"text":"The process is something like sending a fax: The CCK in the intestines cannot cross the blood–brain barrier, but it stimulates cells to release something almost like it.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":55},{"text":"The main signal to end a meal is distension of the stomach.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":168},{"text":"The importance of stomach distension explains why sham feeding does not satisfy hunger, and why eating satisfies your hunger before the nutrition reaches the cells that need it.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":169},{"text":"The duodenum (DYOU-oh-DEE-num or dyuh-ODDehn-uhm), the part of the small intestine adjoining the stomach, is a major site for absorbing nutrients.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":170},{"text":"First, CCK constricts the sphincter muscle between the stomach and the duodenum, causing the stomach to hold its contents and fill more quickly than usual.","printedPage":308,"pdfPage":326,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":171}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Blood-brain the body and the brain’s main fuel.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":57},{"text":"Two pancreatic hormones, insulin and glucagon, regulate the flow of glucose into cells.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":58},{"text":"The brain cells are an exception to this rule, because glucose can enter them without need for insulin.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":59},{"text":"Some of the glucose enters the liver, which converts it to glycogen and stores it.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"As time passes after a meal, the blood glucose level falls, insulin levels drop, glucose enters the cells more slowly, and hunger increases (Figure 9.16).","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":61},{"text":"The pancreas increases release of glucagon , stimulating the liver to convert some of its stored glycogen back to glucose.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"That weight gain is a valuable preparation for a season when the animal will have to survive off its fat reserves.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"In the United States, we tend to blame our autumn weight gain on the Halloween and Thanksgiving holidays, but the real reason may be an evolved drive to","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":64},{"text":"Immediately before a meal (as you react to the sight and smell of the food), as well as during and after a meal, the pancreas releases insulin, which enables glucose to enter the cells.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":172},{"text":"The net effect of insulin prevents blood glucose levels from rising too sharply.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":173},{"text":"In autumn, animals that are preparing for hibernation have constantly high insulin levels.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":174},{"text":"They rapidly deposit much of each meal as fat and glycogen, quickly grow hungry again, and continue gaining weight.","printedPage":309,"pdfPage":327,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":175}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Glucagon","definition":"pancreatic autoimmune attack reduces or eliminates the ability of the pancreas to produce insulin.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"Type 1 diabetes requires treatment by injections or a pump to provide the needed insulin.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"Because the restricted diet is difficult, eating disorders are common, especially for adolescents .","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"Type 2 diabetes , which usually begins in middle age or later, is the more common type.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"In Type 2 diabetes, the pancreas produces enough insulin, but cells have become unresponsive to it.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"Because the cells are starving, hunger increases and eating increases, but the person continues losing weight.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"It also requires the person to maintain a careful diet, minimizing intake of sugars.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":176},{"text":"It occurs mostly in association with obesity and lack of exercise.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":177},{"text":"With either type of diabetes, if untreated, the blood glucose level rises, sometimes to harmful levels, but not much glucose enters the cells.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":178}],"originalFacts":6,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[{"term":"Type 1 diabetes","definition":"impaired glucose absorption caused by low levels of insulin secretion","sourcePrintedPage":634,"sourcePdfPage":652},{"term":"Type 2","definition":"impaired glucose absorption insulin","sourcePrintedPage":634,"sourcePdfPage":652}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":176,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":156},{"id":"bp14-m9-3-h09","title":"Leptin","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m9-3-h04","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"facts":[{"text":"Taste, stomach distension, duodenum distension, and insulin help regulate the onset and offset of a meal.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":73},{"text":"Researchers had long suspected some kind of fat monitoring, but they discovered the actual mechanism by accident.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"After researchers identified the responsible gene, they found the peptide it makes, a previously unknown hormone that they named leptin , from the Greek word leptos, meaning “slender” .","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"Unlike insulin, which is so evolutionarily ancient that we find it throughout the animal kingdom, leptin is limited to vertebrates .","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"Because a mouse with a mutation in the leptin gene does not make leptin, its brain reacts as if its body has no fat stores and must be starving.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"After all, the body makes leptin all the time, so it should have no unpleasant side effects.","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"However, most overweight people already produce plenty of leptin, and giving them extra leptin produces little change in their appetite .","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"However, later research found that extra leptin also produces little effect on normal-weight people.","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"Low levels of leptin trigger hunger, but beyond a certain level, additional leptin has only a slight effect .","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":81},{"text":"When your fat reserves decrease, leptin levels decline, and you react by eating more and becoming less active, to save energy.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":179},{"text":"When leptin levels return to normal, you eat less and become more active.","printedPage":310,"pdfPage":328,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":180},{"text":"As you might imagine, news of this research inspired pharmaceutical companies to hope they could make a fortune by selling leptin.","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":181},{"text":"Leptin does help those rare people who are genetically unable to make .","printedPage":311,"pdfPage":329,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":84},{"text":"People eat more on weekends than on other days, and more when eating .","printedPage":312,"pdfPage":330,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":94},{"text":"Output from the hunger cells also inhibits areas that facilitate .","printedPage":312,"pdfPage":330,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":95},{"text":"Melanocortin receptors in the paraventricular nucleus are important .","printedPage":312,"pdfPage":330,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":96},{"text":"Researchers have not yet found a drug that stimulates melanocortin .","printedPage":315,"pdfPage":333,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":115},{"text":"Rats with similar damage sometimes double or triple their laboratory animals randomly assigned pregnant females to a control diet or a diet that produces world.","printedPage":315,"pdfPage":333,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":191},{"text":"At one time psychologists assumed that obesity was a reaction to psychological distress.","printedPage":315,"pdfPage":333,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":192},{"text":"So, emotions are merely one contributor, and usually not a large one.","printedPage":315,"pdfPage":333,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":193},{"text":"The offspring from obese females developed changes in their hypothalamic anatomy and their insulin responses that increased their own probability of .","printedPage":315,"pdfPage":333,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":126},{"text":"Researchers have identified many other genetic variants that The stomach stores food for a time, and then a round sphincter muscle opens to release food to the small intestine.","The small intestine has enzymes that digest proteins, fats, and carbohydrates.","It absorbs digested materials into the blood, which carries them to cells that either use them or store them. The large intestine absorbs water and minerals and lubricates the remaining materials for excretion.","At about the age of weaning, most mammals lose the intestinal enzyme lactase, which is necessary for metabolizing","Adult mammals can drink a little milk, but consuming too much causes stomach cramps, gas, and diarrhea.","The declining level of lactase may be an evolved mechanism to encourage weaning at the appropriate time. Many adults have enough lactase levels to consume milk and other dairy products throughout life.","However, the prevalence of the necessary genes varies.","Whereas Europeans who can digest lactose in adulthood all have variants of the same gene, people in various parts of Africa have genes that differ from one another and from Europeans, indicating that genes for adult lactose digestion evolved independently several times as groups began domesticating cattle. For other residents of the Americas, the probability of digesting lactose depends on the origins of their ancestors.","Many people have unsubstantiated beliefs, such as the belief that eating sugar makes children hyperactive.","The belief that sugar causes hyperactivity is an illusion based on people’s tendency to see what they expect to see.","Another common misconception is that eating turkey causes sleepiness, supposedly because eating turkey increases the supply of tryptophan, which enables the brain to make serotonin and melatonin.
